paper.title_en: Charged gravitational atoms in Euler–Heisenberg electrodynamics: quasi-bound states of charged particles around black holes
paper.abstract_en: Massive scalar fields can form long-lived clouds outside a black hole, creating a gravitational analog of atomic energy levels. We study such clouds around a charged black hole whose electromagnetic field is modified by Euler–Heisenberg vacuum-polarization effects. We consider both neutral and charged particles, together with different angular and radial excitations. When the particle and black hole have opposite charges, electrostatic attraction strengthens the binding and increases absorption by the horizon. Like charges instead produce more diffuse clouds with energies closer to the rest-mass threshold and substantially longer lifetimes. The nonlinear electromagnetic correction generally weakens the binding and reduces the horizon leakage, although the most weakly bound states are almost insensitive to it. Higher radial levels likewise lie farther from the black hole and decay more slowly. All states found here are decaying, because the localized levels remain well separated from the superradiant frequency range. The particle charge therefore controls the broad organization of the spectrum, while nonlinear vacuum polarization leaves a smaller but systematic imprint on both the level energies and their lifetimes.
